translations.text: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: "Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you."
"The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord and make his paths straight."
Now John the Baptist was in the wilderness, and he preached a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
And all the country of Judea and the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and all were baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
Now John was clothed in camel's hair, and a leather belt was bound around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
And he preached, saying: "After me comes one mightier than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie."
"I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
And it came to pass in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
And immediately, as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened and the Spirit descending upon him like a dove.
And a voice came down from heaven: "You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased."
And immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
And he was there forty days, being tempted by the devil. And he was with the wild beasts, and the angels ministered to him.
Now after John had been handed over to prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of God
and saying: "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe in the gospel."
And as he was passing along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, Simon's brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
And Jesus said to them: "Come, follow me, and I will make you become fishers of men."
And immediately they left their nets and followed him.
And going on a little farther, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were also in the boat mending their nets.
And immediately he called them. And they immediately left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and went after him.
And they went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath he was teaching in the synagogues.
And they were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.
And there was in their synagogue a man possessed by an unclean spirit, and he cried out
and said: "Leave us alone! What is there between us and you, Jesus of Nazareth? You have come to destroy us. I know who you are, the Holy One of God!"
And Jesus rebuked him and said: "Be silent, and come out of him!"
And the unclean spirit convulsed him, and cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
And all were amazed, and they questioned one another and said: "What is this new teaching? For with authority he commands the unclean spirits, and they obey him."
And this report about him went out into all the surrounding villages of Galilee.
And immediately they came out of the synagogue and came to the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Now Simon's mother-in-law lay sick with a fever. And immediately they told him about her.
And he came, took her by the hand and raised her up, and the fever left her, and she served them.
And when it was evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all the sick and those possessed by demons.
And the whole city was gathered before the door.
And he healed many who were sick with various diseases and cast out many demons; and he did not allow the demons to speak, for they knew him, that he is the Christ.
And very early in the morning he rose, went out, and went to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
And Simon and those who were with him followed him.
And when they found him, they said to him: "Everyone is looking for you."
And he said to them: "Come, let us go around also to the neighbouring towns and cities, so that I may preach there too, for this is why I have come."
And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee and cast out demons.
And a leper came to him, begging him, and kneeling down he said to him: "If you will, you are able to cleanse me."
And Jesus had compassion on him, stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him: "I will; be cleansed!"
And as soon as he had said this to him, immediately the leprosy left him and he was cleansed.
And he spoke sternly to him, and immediately sent him away,
and said to him: "Tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."

But when he went out, he began to proclaim it widely and to spread the news around, so that Jesus could no longer openly enter a city, but stayed outside in deserted places. And people came to him from everywhere.
And after some days he came again to Capernaum, and it was heard that he was in the house.
And many gathered, so that there was no longer room for them, not even outside the door, and he spoke the word to them.
And they came to him, bringing to him a paralysed man, carried by four men.
And since they could not get near him because of the crowd, they tore open the roof of the house in which he was, dug through it, and let down the bed on which the paralysed man lay.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralysed man: "Child, your sins are forgiven you!"
Some of the scribes were sitting there, and they were reasoning in their hearts:
"Why does this man speak blasphemy like this? Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
At once Jesus knew in his spirit that they were reasoning this way in their hearts. He said to them, "Why do you reason like this in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say to the paralysed man, 'Your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Get up, take up your bed and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — he said to the paralysed man,
"I say to you: get up, take up your bed and go to your house!"
At once he got up, took up the bed and went out in front of everyone. They were amazed, and they glorified God and said, "We have never seen anything like this."
Then he went out again beside the sea, and the whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
As he was passing on from there, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, "Follow me!" And he got up and followed him.

And it happened that as he reclined at table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and with his disciples, for there were many of them there, and they were following him.
When the scribes of the Pharisees saw that he was eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, "Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are sick do. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
The disciples of John and of the Pharisees were fasting, and they said to him, "Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?"
Jesus said to them, "Can the children of the wedding fast while the bridegroom is still with them? As long as the bridegroom is still with them, they cannot fast.
But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days.
No one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise the new patch pulls away its fill from the old, and the tear becomes worse.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine bursts the skins, the wine is spilled and the skins are ruined. Rather, new wine is poured into new wineskins."
And it happened that as he was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, his disciples began, as they went along, to pluck the heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, "Look, what they are doing on the Sabbath is not lawful!"
He said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and he and those with him were hungry?

How he went into the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the bread of the offering, which it was not lawful for anyone but the priests to eat, and he also gave some to those who were with him?"
And he said to them, "The Sabbath was created for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath."
Again he went into the synagogue, and there was a man there whose hand was withered.
They were watching him to see whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
And he said to the man whose hand was withered: "Come forward into the middle!"
And he said to them: "What is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil? To save a life, or to destroy it?" But they were silent.
And he looked at them with anger, grieved at the blindness of their heart, and said to the man: "Stretch out your hand!" And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored to life.
And the Pharisees went out at once with the Herodians and took counsel about him, how they might destroy him.
But Jesus went away with his disciples toward the sea; and a great multitude from Galilee and from Judea
and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and from beyond the Jordan, and from the region of Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing how much he was doing, had come to him.
And he told his disciples to keep a small boat waiting for him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush him.
For he had healed many, so that those who were afflicted even pressed upon him, that they might only touch him [?].
And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, would fall down before him, crying out and saying: "You are the Son of God."
And he would rebuke them sharply, so that they would not make him known.
And he went up into the mountains and called those whom he wanted; and they came to him.
And he appointed twelve, so that they might be with him, and he gave them the name apostles, and so that he might send them out to preach,
and that they might have authority to cast out demons.
And he gave Simon the name Peter,
and James son of Zebedee and John the brother of James, and he gave them the name Boanerges, which means "sons of thunder";
and Andrew and Philip, Bartholomew and Matthew the tax collector, and Thomas and James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
And they came home, and again the crowd gathered, so that they did not have time even to eat bread.
And when his own people heard of it, they went out to seize him, for they were saying: "He is out of his mind."
And the scribes who had come from Jerusalem were saying: "Beelzebul is with him, and by the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons."
And he called them to him and spoke to them in parables: "How can the devil cast out the devil?
And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
And if the devil casts out the devil and is divided against himself, he can no longer stand, but has come to an end.
Nor can anyone enter the house of a strong man and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man; only then will he plunder his house.
Truly I tell you that all sins will be forgiven the sons of men, and all blasphemies, however much they blaspheme;
but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven, but will be guilty of an eternal sin.
For they had said, "He has an unclean spirit."
And his brothers and his mother came, and they stood outside and sent in to him to call him.
And a crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him, "Look, your mother and your brothers are looking for you."
He answered them and said, "Who is my mother, or my brothers?"
And he looked around at his disciples who were sitting around him and said, "Here are my mother and my brothers!
For whoever does the will of God is my brother and my sister and my mother."
Again he began to teach by the seashore. And a great crowd gathered to him, and he got into a boat and sat in it on the sea, and the whole crowd was with him beside the sea, on the land.
And he taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:
"Listen! Look, a sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it.
And other seed fell on rocky ground, where there was not much depth of soil, and it sprang up at once, because it had no depth.
But when the sun rose, it was scorched, because it had not put down roots, and it withered.
And other seed fell among thorns; the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
And other seed fell on good ground and yielded fruit, springing up and growing, and one bore thirty, and one sixty, and one a hundred."
And he said, "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!"
Then when he was alone, those who were around him, together with the Twelve, asked him about the parables.
And he said to them, "To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to those outside everything is spoken in parables,
so that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they turn and be forgiven."
And he said to them, "Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?
The sower sows the word.
And these are the ones along the path, where the word is sown: when they hear it, the devil comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
And these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy;
but they have no root in themselves and last only a short time; then, when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.
And those that were sown among the thorns are these: those who hear the word,
and the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of wealth, which enter in, choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And these are the ones that were sown on the good ground: those who hear the word and receive it and bring forth fruit: one thirtyfold, one sixtyfold, and one a hundredfold.
And he said to them: Does anyone bring a lamp and put it under a bushel, or under a bed? Is it not so that it may be set on a lampstand?
For there is no secret that will not be made manifest, nor is there anything hidden that will not come to light.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And he said to them: Take heed what you hear, for with the measure with which you measure, with the same it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you who hear.
Whoever has, to him more will be given; and whoever has not, even what he has will be taken from him.
And he said: So is the kingdom of God, as when a man sows seed upon the earth
and he sleeps and rises, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, he knows not how,
for of itself the earth brings forth fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain of wheat in the ear.
But when the fruit is ripe, he immediately sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come.
And he said: How shall we liken the kingdom of God? Or with what parable shall we set it forth?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown upon the earth, is the smallest of all the seeds that are on the earth.
And when it is sown, it springs up and becomes greater than all the herbs and puts forth great branches, so that even the birds of heaven are able to settle under its shadow.
And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as much as they were able to hear.
And without a parable he said nothing to them; but privately he explained everything to his own disciples.
And on that day, when evening had come, he said to them: Come, let us cross over to the other side.
And they left the crowd and took him along, just as he was, in the boat,
and there arose a great storm of wind, and it was pouring the waves into the boat, so that it was nearly filled.
But he himself was lying at the head end, on a pillow. And they woke him and said to him: Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?
And he awoke and rebuked the wind and the sea and said: Be silent and close your mouth! And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them: Why are you so faint-hearted, and do you still have no faith?
And they were afraid with a great fear and said: Who then is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?
And he crossed over from there to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gergesenes.
And as he came out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs to meet him,
who lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him any longer, not even with chains.
For he had burst and smashed the many fetters and chains with which they had bound him, and no one was able to subdue him.
And always, day and night, he was among the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and bruising himself with stones.
And when he saw Jesus from far off, he ran and bowed down before him,
and cried out with a loud voice and said: "What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I adjure you by God, do not torment me!"
For he was saying to him: "Come out of that man, unclean spirit!"
And he asked him: "What is your name?" And he said to him: "Legion is my name, for we are many."
And he begged him earnestly not to send them out of the country.
And a large herd of pigs was there, feeding on the mountainside.
And they begged him and said: "Send us into those pigs, so that we may go into them."

And Jesus gave them the command. And those unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs. And the herd rushed down the cliff toward the sea; there were about two thousand of them, and they drowned in the sea.
But the swineherds fled and told it in the city and in the countryside. And people came out to see what had happened.
And they came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man, the one who had had the Legion, sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
And those who had seen it told them what had happened to the demon-possessed man and about the pigs.
And they began to beg him to leave their region.
And as he was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged him.
And he did not allow him, but said to him: "Go home to your own people and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and that he had mercy on you."
And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and everyone was amazed.
And when Jesus had crossed over again to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him. And he was by the seashore.
And behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue came, whose name was Jairus; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet.
And he begged him earnestly, saying: "My daughter is dying. Come and lay your hand on her, so that she may be saved and live."
And he went with him. And a large crowd followed him and pressed in on him.
And there was a certain woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years.
And she had suffered greatly at the hands of many physicians and had spent everything she had, and had not been helped at all, but had grown even worse.
When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his garment.
For she was saying in her heart: "If I only touch his garment, I will be saved."
And at once the flow of her blood dried up, and she felt in her body that she had been healed of her affliction.
And at once Jesus knew in his heart that power had gone out from him, and he turned to the crowd and said: "Who touched my garment?"
And his disciples said to him: "Do you see this crowd pressing in on you, and yet you say, 'Who touched my garment?'"
And Jesus kept looking around to see who had done this.
But the woman was afraid and trembled because of what she had done in secret. She understood what had happened to her, and she came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
And Jesus said to her: "Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace, and be well, free from your affliction."
While he was still saying this, some people came from the house of the ruler of the synagogue and said: "Your daughter has died. Why do you trouble the teacher any further?"
But when Jesus heard what was said, he said to the ruler of the synagogue: "Do not be afraid; only believe!"
And he allowed no one to follow him except Peter and James and John, the brother of James.
And they came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and he saw an uproar, and people weeping and wailing loudly.
And he went in and said to them: "Why are you in an uproar, and why are you weeping? The child is not dead, but sleeping."
And they laughed at him. But he put them all out, and took the child's father and her mother and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.
And he took the child by the hand and said to her: "Talitha kum!", which means: "Little girl, I say to you, arise!"

And at once the girl got up and walked, for she was about twelve years old. And they were amazed: [?] the carpenter [?], the son of Mary, and the brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us? And they took offense at him.
And he strictly ordered them that no one should know of it, and he told them to give her bread.
And he went out from there and came to his own home town, and his disciples followed him.

And when it was the Sabbath, he began to teach in their synagogue. And many who heard him marveled at his teaching and said: "Where does this man come from? What is this wisdom that has been given to him, and these mighty works that are done by his hands?"
"Is he not the carpenter, the son of Mary, and the brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?" And they took offense at him.
But Jesus said to them: "A prophet is not without honor except in his own home town and among his own relatives."
And he was not able to do even one mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
And he marveled at their unbelief, and he went around the villages in the area, teaching.
And he called the Twelve and began to send them out two by two, and he gave them authority over unclean spirits.
And he ordered them to take nothing with them for the journey except a staff only: no bag, no bread, and no copper money in their belts.
But let them wear sandals, and do not put on two tunics.
And he said to them: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that place.
And whatever place does not receive you or listen to you, when you leave that place, shake off the dust that is under your feet as a testimony against them.
And they went out and preached that people should repent.
And they cast out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil, and they were healed.
And King Herod heard of it, for the name of Jesus had become known, and he said: John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work through him.
But others said: He is Elijah. Some said: He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.
When Herod heard this, he said: John, whom I beheaded, he has risen.
For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.
For John had been saying to Herod: It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife as your wife.
And Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, because he knew in his heart that the man was righteous and holy, and he protected him. He would listen to him and do many things, and he heeded him gladly.
And an opportune day came, when Herod, on his birthday, held a feast for the rich men, the commanders of thousands, and the leaders of Galilee.
And the daughter of Herodias came in and danced, and she pleased Herod and his fellow diners. He said to the girl: Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.
And he swore to her: Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.
And she went out and said to her mother: What shall I ask him for? And she said to her: The head of John the Baptist.
And at once she went back in to the king in haste and said to him: I want you to give me, right now, the head of John the Baptist on a platter.
And the king was grieved, but because of his oath and because of the guests he did not go back on his word to her.
And at once the king sent an executioner and ordered him to cut off his head.
And he went and cut off his head in the prison, and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
And when his disciples heard of it, they came and wrapped his body and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gathered around Jesus and told him everything, all that they had done and taught.
And he said to them: Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little! For there were many people coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
And they went away by boat to a deserted place by themselves.
And many people saw them going and recognized them. They ran there on foot from all the towns, gathered, and got there ahead of them.
And he came out and saw a great crowd, and he had mercy on them, because they were like sheep that have no shepherd. And he began to teach them much.
And when much time had passed, his disciples came to him and said to him: "This place is a desert, and much time has passed.
Send them away, so that they may go to the surrounding farms and villages and buy themselves something to eat."
But he answered and said to them: "You give them something to eat." And they said to him: "Shall we go and buy two hundred drachmas' worth of bread and give it to them to eat?"
He said to them: "How many loaves do you have? Go and see!" And when they had seen, they told him: "Five loaves and two fish."
And he commanded them to make everyone sit down in companies, group by group, on the green grass.
And they sat down in rows [?], by hundreds and by fifties.

And he took the five loaves of bread and the two fish, and he looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and he divided the two fish among them all.
And they all ate and were filled.
And they took up the leftover fragments, twelve baskets, and of the fish as well.
And those who ate the bread were five thousand men.
And immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead to Bethsaida, while he sent the crowd away.
And when he himself had parted from the crowd, he went up onto the mountain to pray.
And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
And he saw them distressed by the tossing of the boat, for the wind was against them. And about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea, and he meant to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was some apparition, and they cried out.
For they all saw him and were terrified. And immediately he began to speak to them and said to them: "Be steadfast, it is I, do not be afraid!"
And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased. And they were exceedingly amazed in their hearts.
For they had not understood about the loaves, because their hearts were hardened.
And they crossed over to land and came to Gennesaret.
And when they got out of the boat, the people of that place immediately recognized him.
And they ran about all the surrounding villages and began to carry the sick around on beds wherever they heard that he was there.
And whatever villages, or cities, or farms he entered, they would lay the sick in the streets and beg him that they might touch just the hem of his garment. And as many as touched him were healed.
And the scribes and Pharisees gathered to him, some of whom had come from Jerusalem.
Some of them saw that certain of his disciples were eating bread uncleanly, with unwashed hands, and they reproached them,
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat bread unless they wash their hands often [?], because they hold to the tradition of their priests.
And when they come in from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other things they have learned to keep: the washing of cups and jugs and kettles and beds.
Then the Pharisees and the scribes asked him: "Why do your disciples not live by the tradition of the priests, but eat bread with unwashed hands?"
He answered them: "Isaiah prophesied well about you, you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honours me only with their lips, but their heart is far removed from me.'"
"'They serve me in vain, for they teach human teachings and commandments.'"
"For you have abandoned the commandment of God and hold to human teaching."
And he said to them: "You do well at setting aside the commandment of God so that you can establish your own commandment."
"For Moses told you: 'Honour your father and your mother,' and 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must surely be put to death.'"
"But you say: If a man says to his father or his mother, 'Corban' (that is, a gift), 'is whatever you would have gained from me,'
"then you no longer let him do anything for his father or mother."
"You have made the word of God worthless by the teaching that you teach, and you do many other things like these [?]."
And he called all the people to him and said to them: "Listen to me, all of you, and understand."
"Nothing that goes into a person from outside can defile him. What comes out of him is what defiles a person."
And when he left the people and went into a house, his disciples asked him about the parable.
And he said to them: "Are you also still without understanding like this? Do you not yet understand that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile him?"
"For it does not go into his heart but into his belly, and it goes out into the drain, and so all foods are made clean."
And he said to them: "What comes out of a person is what defiles the person."
"For from within, from the heart of people, come evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, thefts, murders,
"greed, wickedness, deceit, impurity, an evil eye, blasphemy, arrogance, and foolishness."
"All these evils come from within and defile a person."
And he got up and left there and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon. He went into a house and did not want anyone to know he was there, but he could not stay hidden.
A woman whose daughter was tormented by a demon heard about him, and she fell at his feet.
The woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by birth, and she begged him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
And Jesus said to her: "Let the children be fed first, for it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
She answered him: "Yes, Lord, but even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
But Jesus said to her: "Because of this word, go! The demon has gone out of your daughter."
And she went to her house and found that the demon had gone out, and the daughter lying on the bed.
And again he went out from the region of Tyre and Sidon and came to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of the Decapolis.
And those who had brought a mute boy begged him to lay his hand on him.
And he took him out from the crowd, alone, and placed his fingers on him, and spat into his ears, and touched his tongue.
And he looked up to heaven, sighed, and said to him: "Ephphatha!", which means: "Be opened."
And immediately his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke correctly.
And he commanded them to tell no one. But the more he commanded them, the more they proclaimed it.
And they were utterly amazed and said: "He has done all things well, for he makes the deaf hear and the mute speak."
In those days there was again a great crowd, and they had nothing to eat. He called his disciples and said to them:
"I have compassion on this crowd, because for three days now they have stayed with me, and they have nothing to eat.
And if I send them away to their homes fasting, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come from far away."
His disciples said to him: "How will you be able to satisfy them with bread here in the wilderness?"
And he asked them: "How many loaves do you have?" And they said: "Seven."
And he commanded the crowd to sit down [?] on the ground. And he took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and they set them before the crowd.
And they also had a few fish, and he blessed these too and ordered that they be set before them.
And they ate and were satisfied; and they took up the leftover broken pieces, seven full baskets.
For those who ate were about four thousand. And he sent them away.
And immediately he got into the boat with his disciples and came to the region of Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came out and began to question him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, for they were testing him.
And he sighed deeply in his spirit and said: "Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I tell you: no sign will be given to this generation."
And he left them, got into the boat again, and crossed over to the other side.
And they had forgotten to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
And he commanded them, saying: "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the [?] of the Herodians."
And they reasoned in their hearts and said to one another: "We have no bread."

And Jesus understood, and he said to them: "Why are you reasoning that it is because we have no bread, you of little faith? Do you not yet know, and have you not understood? Are your hearts still hardened?
You have eyes and do not see, and you have ears and do not hear. And do you not remember,
when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments did you pick up?" They said to him: "Twelve."
"And then, when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many hampers full of leftovers did you pick up?" And they said to him: "Seven."
And he said to them: "How is it that you have not understood?"
And they came to Bethsaida, and they brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him with his hand.
And he took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. He spat on his eyes, laid his hands on him, and asked him: "Do you see anything?"
He looked up and said: "I see people like trees, walking."
Then he laid his hands on his eyes again, and he looked up with his sight settled and saw everything completely.
And he sent him away to his house and said to him: "Do not even go into the village."
And Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, saying: "What do people say about me? Who am I?"
They answered him and said: "John the Baptist"; and others say "Elijah"; and some say "one of the prophets."
He said to them: "And you, what do you say? Who am I?" Peter answered him and said: "You are the Christ."
He sternly warned them to tell no one about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer much and be despised, be killed by the elders, the chief priests and the scribes, and rise on the third day.
And he spoke this word openly. And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
But he turned around and looked at his disciples, rebuked Peter, and said: "Get away from me, devil, for you are not thinking the things of God, but the things of men."
And he called the crowd together with his disciples and said to them: "Whoever wishes to walk in my footsteps, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his own life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the sake of this gospel will save it.
For what profit is it to a person if he gains the whole world and forfeits his soul?
Or what can a person give in exchange for his soul?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels."
And he said to them: "Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God come with power."
And after six days Jesus took Peter, James and John, led them up a high mountain by themselves, and was transfigured before them.
And his clothing became shining and exceedingly white, so white that no fuller on earth could bleach it like that.
And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were standing and talking with Jesus.
And Peter answered and said to Jesus: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
For he did not know what he should answer, because they were terrified.
And there was a cloud overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud: "This is my beloved Son; listen to him!"
And suddenly they looked around and no longer saw anyone, except Jesus alone with them.
And as they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them not to tell anyone what they had seen, except when the Son of Man should rise from the dead.
And they kept that saying, and questioned among themselves: "What is this: 'when he rises from the dead'?"
They asked him and said: "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
And he answered and said to them: "Elijah will indeed come first and restore all things; and how is it written of the Son of Man, that he must suffer much and be treated with contempt?
But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wished, as it is written of him."
And when they came to the disciples, they saw a crowd around them, and the scribes were pressing upon them, disputing with them.
And immediately, when all the crowd saw him, they were amazed, and they ran up and greeted him.
And he asked them: "What are you arguing about with one another?"
And one of the crowd answered and said: "Teacher, I brought my son to you, who has a mute spirit.
And wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and wastes away. And I told your disciples to drive it out, and they could not."
And he answered and said to them: "O faithless generation! How long shall I be with you? Bring him to me!"
And they brought him to him. And when he saw him, immediately the spirit threw him into convulsions; and when he fell on the ground, he rolled about and foamed.
And he asked his father: "How long has it been since this came upon him?" And he said: "From childhood.
And many times it throws him into fire and into water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help us and have mercy on us."
And Jesus said to him: "If you can! All things are possible for one who believes."
And at once the father of the child cried out and said: "I believe; help my unbelief."
When Jesus saw that the crowd was gathering to him, he rebuked the spirit and said to it: "I say to you, mute and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again!"
And it cried out greatly, convulsed him, and came out; and he became like a dead man, so that many even said, "He has died."
But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up, and he stood up.
And when he had gone into the house, his disciples asked him privately: "Why could we not drive it out?"
And he said to them: This kind goes out by nothing except prayer.
And as they were going out from there, they passed through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know it,
for he was teaching the disciples and saying to them: The Son of Man is to be handed over into the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when they have killed him, on the third day he will rise.
But they did not understand that saying, and they were afraid to ask him.
And he came to Capernaum. When he had gone into the house, he asked them: What were you saying to one another on the way?
But they were silent, because on the way they had been saying to one another: Who is greater?
And he sat down and called the Twelve and said to them: Whoever wishes to be first, let him be last of all and servant of all.
And he brought a child and set him in their midst, and he took him in his arms and said to them:
Whoever receives one of such children receives me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.
John answered him and said: Teacher, we saw someone who was casting out demons in your name, who does not follow with us, and we tried to stop him.
But Jesus said: Do not stop him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name and be able to speak evil of me.
For whoever is not an enemy to us is on our side.
And whoever gives you a cup of water to drink for the sake of the name, because you belong to Christ, truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.
And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be far better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is better for you to enter life with one hand than to have two hands and go into that unquenchable fire.
And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and go into Gehenna.
And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out: it is better to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and go into Gehenna,
where their worm does not die and their fire is not quenched.
For everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good; but if salt loses its taste, with what will it be salted? Have salt, and keep peace with one another.
And he got up from there and came to the region of Judea beyond the Jordan, and a large crowd went along with him, and, as was his custom, he taught them.
And Pharisees came up to him and asked him: Is it lawful for a husband to divorce his wife? For they were testing him.
He answered and said to them: What did Moses command you?
And they said: Moses ordered that a certificate of divorce be written and that she be sent away.
Jesus answered and said to them: Because of the hardness of your hearts he wrote this commandment.
But from the beginning of creation God made them male and female, and said:
"For this reason each man shall leave his father and his mother and shall be joined to his wife,
and the two shall be one flesh." From now on they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Now what God has joined together, let no man separate.
And afterwards, in the house, his disciples asked him about this.
And he said to them: "If a woman leaves her husband and becomes the wife of another, she commits adultery.
And if a man leaves his wife and takes another as wife, he commits adultery."
And they were bringing children to him, so that he might lay his hand on them; but the disciples were rebuking those who brought them.
When Jesus saw this, he rebuked them and said to them: "Let those children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I say to you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it."
And he took them in his arms, laid his hand on them, and blessed them.
And as he was going out on the road, a certain man ran up, knelt before him, begged him and asked him: "Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?"
But Jesus said to him: "Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honour your father and your mother."
But he answered and said to him: "Teacher, I have done all these things from my youth."

And Jesus looked at him and loved him, and said to him: "One thing you still lack: go, sell whatever you have and give it to the poor, and you will receive treasure in heaven; and take up the cross, come, and follow me."
But he was grieved at that word and went away sorrowful, for he was very rich.
And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples: "How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!"
And his disciples were astonished at his word; but Jesus answered again and said to them: "Children, how hard it is for those who trust in wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
And they were even more amazed, and said to one another: "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said to them: "With men it is impossible, but not so with God; for all things are possible with God."
Peter began to say to him: "Look, we have left everything and followed you."
Jesus answered him and said: "Truly I say to you: there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or fields for my sake or for the sake of this gospel
who will not receive a hundredfold now in this time: houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions, and in the age to come eternal life."
For many who are first will be last, and the last first.

And they were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus went ahead of them. They were amazed, and they followed him and were afraid. And again he took the twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to him afterwards,
saying: "Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the gentiles.
And they will mock him and torment him and spit on him, and they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise."
And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him and said to him: "Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you."
And he said to them: "What do you want me to do for you?"
They said to him: "Grant us that we may sit at your right and at your left in your glory."
Jesus answered and said to them: "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I am to drink, or [be baptized with] the baptism with which I am to be baptized?"
They said to him: "We can." Jesus said to them: "The cup that I am to drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am to be baptized you will be baptized,
but to sit at my right and at my left is not mine to give; rather, it is for those for whom it has been prepared."
And when the ten heard it, they began to be angry with James and John.
But he called them and said to them: "You know that those who are thought to rule over the gentiles lord it over them, and the rich exercise authority over them.
But it shall not be so among you; rather, whoever wishes to be great among you, let him be your servant;
and whoever of you wishes to be first, let him be the slave of all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served by anyone, but to serve and to give his own life as a ransom for many."
And they came to Jericho. And as he was going out of Jericho with his disciples and a great crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind man, was sitting by the road begging.
And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say: "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Many rebuked him, so that he would be silent; but he cried out [?] all the more and said: "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
And Jesus stood still and said to call him. And they called the blind man and said to him: "Get up, do not be afraid, he is calling you [?]."
He threw off his cloak, got up, and came to Jesus.
And Jesus answered him and said: "What do you want me to do for you?" And the blind man said to him: "Rabboni, that I may see again."
And he said: "Go, your faith has saved you." And immediately he regained his sight and followed him.
And when they drew near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, close by the Mount of Olives, he sent two of the disciples
and said to them: "Go to the village that is opposite you; and immediately, as you enter there, you will find a colt tied, on which no one has ever sat; untie it and bring it to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, say to them: 'Its lord needs it, and he will soon send it back here.'"
They went and found a colt tied at the door, outside in the street, and they were untying it.
And some of those standing there said to them: "What are you doing? Why are you untying that colt?"
But they told them what Jesus had commanded them, and they let them go.
And they brought the colt to Jesus. They put their garments on it, and he sat on it.
And many spread their garments on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
And those who went in front and those who followed behind were crying out and saying: "Glory in the highest! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming! Peace in the heavens and glory in the highest!"
And he entered Jerusalem, into the temple [?] ... he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
And [?] and he was hungry.
And he saw [?] ... in leaf, and he came to see whether he might find something [on it]. When he came, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
He answered and [?] "From you let no one [?] ..." [?]
He entered the temple [?] ... in the [?], and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those who sold doves.
And he would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
And he was teaching them and saying to them: "It is written: 'My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations.' But you have made it a den of robbers."
And the chief priests and the scribes heard it, and they were looking for a way to destroy him; for they were afraid of him, because all the people were amazed at his teaching.
And whenever evening came, they would go out of the city.
And as they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
And Peter remembered and said to him: "Teacher, look, the fig tree that you cursed has withered."
Jesus answered and said to him:
"If you have faith in God, truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, 'Be uprooted and thrown into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says will happen ..."
"Therefore I tell you: whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours."
"And when you stand up to pray, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your sins."
And they came again to Jerusalem. And as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes and the elders came to him
and said to him: "By what authority are you doing this, and who gave you this authority?"
But Jesus answered and said to them: "If you will, let me also ask you one question. Answer me, and I too will tell you by what authority I do this."
"The baptism of John: was it from heaven, or from men? Tell me."
And they reasoned with one another, saying: "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
But if we say, 'From men'..." They were afraid of the people, for everyone held John to be a prophet, because he truly was a prophet.
And they answered Jesus and said: "We do not know." And Jesus answered and said to them: "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
And he began to speak to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress, built a tower, leased it to tenants and went away.
And at the season he sent a servant to the tenants, to receive from them the fruit of the vineyard.
But they seized him, beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
And again he sent them another servant, and they sent him away too, shamefully treated.
And again he sent another, and they killed him; and many others as well: some they beat, and some they killed.
He still had one son, his beloved. Last of all he sent him to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
But when the tenants saw him coming to them, they said, 'This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'
And they seized him, killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
What then will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy those tenants of the vineyard and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not even read this scripture: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner'?"
this was from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"
And they sought to seize him, but they were afraid of the people, for they understood that he had told this parable against them. And they left him and went away.
And they sent to him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to trap him in his words.

When they came, they began to question him with guile and said to him: "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and do not worry about anyone's opinion, for you do not show partiality to any person but truly teach the way of God. Now tell us: is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or should we not pay it?"
But he knew their guile and said to them: "Why are you testing me, you deceivers? Bring me a denarius so that I may look at it."
And they brought one. And he said to them: "Whose image and inscription is this?" They said to him: "Caesar's."
And Jesus answered and said to them: "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's." And they were amazed at him.
And Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying:
"Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone's brother dies and leaves a wife but no child, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, died and left no heir.
The second took her, and he too died, and he also left no heir; and the third did the same.
None of the seven left an heir. Last of all the woman died too.
In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife among them will she be? For all seven had her as wife.
Jesus answered and said to them: Is it not for this reason that you go astray, because you know neither the Scripture nor the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like the angels in heaven.
And as for the dead, that they rise: have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him and said: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. So you are greatly mistaken.
And one of the scribes, who had heard their argument, came up to him. When he saw that he had answered them well, he asked him: Which is the first commandment?
Jesus said to him: The first of all is: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind. This is the first commandment.
And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbour as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these.
And the scribe said to him: Well said, Teacher; you have spoken truly, that he is one, and there is no other besides him;
and to love him with all the heart, and with all the strength, and with all the understanding, and to love one's neighbour as oneself, is greater than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.
And when Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of God. And no one dared to question him any more.
And Jesus answered and said, while teaching in the temple: How do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
For David himself said by the Holy Spirit: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool under your feet.
David himself calls him Lord; so how is he his son? And the great crowd listened to him eagerly.
And he said to them in his teaching: Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in fine clothing and seek greetings in the marketplaces,
and the first seats in the synagogues and the [?] places at banquets;
who devour the houses of widows and for a pretence pray at great length. These will receive the greater condemnation.
Jesus stood opposite the treasury and watched how the people put money into the treasury. And many rich people put in a great deal.
And a poor widow came and put in two mites, which make one quadrans.
And he called his disciples to him and said to them: Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more into this treasury than all of them.
For they all gave out of their surplus, but she, out of her want, gave everything she had, she gave her whole living.
And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him: Teacher, look, what stones these are and what buildings!
And Jesus answered and said to them: Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left upon another that will not be thrown down.
And as he sat on the Mount of Olives, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately:
Tell us, when will this be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?
For many will come in my name and say, 'I am he,' and they will lead many astray.
But when you hear of war and the sound of battle, do not be alarmed, for it must happen, but the end is not yet.
Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom; and there will be earthquakes in place after place, and famine and plague. But these are the beginning of the birth pains.
And they will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will beat you, and they will bring you before judges and kings as a testimony to them and to all the nations.
But first this gospel must be preached.
And when they bring you and hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say; but whatever is given to you in that hour, say that, for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise up against their parents and have them put to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name; but whoever endures to the end will be saved.
But when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it ought not to be — let the one who reads understand — then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
And let those who are on the roofs not come down into the house, nor go in to take anything from their house.
Let the one who is out in the field not turn back to take his garment.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days.
But pray that your flight may not be in winter.
For those days will be days of tribulation such as has not been from the beginning, since God created, until now, nor ever will be again.
And if he had not shortened those days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the elect, whom he chose, he has shortened those days.
And then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ,' or 'Look, there,' do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will perform signs and wonders to lead astray, if they could, even the elect.
But you, be on your guard; for behold, I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light;
and the stars will be falling from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with great power and glory.
And then he will send out his angels and gather his elect from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
Now learn this parable from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and it puts forth leaves, you know that summer [?] is near.
So also you, when you see all these things, understand that it is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But about that day and hour no one knows, not the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father alone.
So watch, stay awake and worship, because you do not know when that time will come.
It is like a man going on a journey: he leaves his house, gives authority to his servants, gives each one his own work, and commands the doorkeeper to stay awake.
So stay awake, because you do not know when the master of the house will come: in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or at dawn;
in case he comes suddenly and finds you asleep.
What I say to you, I say to all: stay awake.
The feast of the Passover was to come after two days. The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to seize him by treachery and kill him.
They said: "Not during this feast, in case there is a riot among the people."
While he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, and was reclining at table, a woman came who had [?] precious ointment of nard, of great price. She took it and poured it on his head.
But some people there were indignant and said to one another: "Why was this waste made?"
"This ointment ought to have been sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor." And they were angry with her.
But Jesus said to them: "Leave her alone and do not trouble her, for she has done a good deed for me.
For the poor are always with you, and whenever you wish, you are able to do good to them; but I am not always with you.
She has done what she could: she has anointed my body with ointment beforehand, to clothe it for burial.
And truly I tell you: wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what this woman has done will also be told in memory of her."
Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests in order to hand him over to them.
When they heard it they rejoiced and promised to give him silver. And he was looking for a way to hand him over at a convenient opportunity.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they slaughtered the Passover lamb, his disciples said to him: "Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?"
He sent two of his disciples and said to them: "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him, and wherever he goes in,
say to the master of that house: 'The Teacher says: Where is my lodging, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?'
He will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there."
The disciples went off to prepare it. They went into the city and found things just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When evening came, he came with the Twelve.
And as they were reclining at table and eating, Jesus said to them: "Truly I tell you: one of you who is eating with me will betray me."
But they began to be troubled and to say to him, one by one: "Surely it is not I, Lord?" And another: "Surely it is not I?"
But he answered and said to them: "One of the twelve, the one who dips into the dish with me, he will betray me."
"For the Son of Man is going as it is written of him; but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for him if that man had not been born."
And while they were still eating, he took bread, blessed it, broke it, gave it to them, and said: "Take; this is my body!"
And he took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them: "This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many."
"Truly I tell you, I will not drink again of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
And they gave thanks and went out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus said to them: "All of you will stumble because of me this night, for it is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'"
"But after I rise, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
But Peter answered and said to him: "Even if all stumble, yet I will not."
And Jesus said to him: "Truly I tell you, today, this very night, before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times."
But Peter spoke all the more vehemently [?]: "Even if I must die with you, I will never deny you." And all of them said the same.
And they came to a village whose name was Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples: "Sit here while I pray."
And he took Peter and James and John with him, and began to be anxious and distressed.
And he said to them: "My soul is deeply grieved, even to death. Wait here and keep watch!"
And he went on a little way, fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, that hour might pass from him.
And he said: "Abba, Father, all things are possible for you; take this cup away from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will."
And he came and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter: "Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?"
"Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak."
And again he went away and prayed, and said the same words.
And he came back and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.
And he came the third time and said to them: "Sleep on now and take your rest. It is finished; the hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners."
"Get up, let us go. Behold, my betrayer has come near."
And while he was still saying this, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
And his betrayer had given them a sign and said to them: "The one I greet is the man. Seize him and lead him away under guard."
And at once he came up to him and said to him: "Teacher!" And he greeted him.
And they laid their hands on him and seized him.
And one of those standing with him drew a sword and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
Jesus answered and said to them: "Have you come out with swords and clubs to seize me as if against a robber?
Every day I was with you in the temple, teaching you, and you did not seize me. But this is so that the writings of the prophets may be fulfilled."
And they all left him and fled.
And a certain young man was following him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body. And the young men seized him.
But he left the linen cloth behind and fled from them naked.
And they led him to Caiaphas the high priest. And the chief priests, the elders and the scribes gathered with him.
And Peter followed him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. He sat with the servants and warmed himself at the fire.
And the chief priests and the whole council were looking for testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death, and they found none.
For many gave false testimony against him, and their testimony did not agree.
And some stood up and gave false testimony against him, and they say [?] the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.
saying: "We heard him say: 'I will destroy this temple made with hands, and on the third day I will build another, not made with hands.'"
And even so their testimony did not agree.
And the high priest stood up among them, questioned Jesus and said to him: "Do you answer nothing to what these men testify against you?"
But he was silent and answered them nothing. Then the high priest questioned him a second time and said to him: "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
And Jesus answered and said to him: "You have said that I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven."
And the high priest tore his tunic and said: "What further need do we have of witnesses?
You have all heard his blasphemy. What do you think?" And they all condemned him and declared him deserving of death.
And some began to spit in his face, and they covered his face with [?], and beat him and said to him: "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?" And the servants struck him on the cheek.
And Peter was in the courtyard. One of the high priest's maidservants came.
And she saw him warming himself, looked at him and said to him: "You too were with Jesus the Nazarene."
But he denied it and said to her: "I neither know nor understand what you are saying." And he went out into the outer courtyard.
And the maidservant saw him and began to say to those who were standing there: "This man is one of them."
But he denied it. And after a little while those who were standing around him said to Peter: "Truly you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean."
But he began to curse and to swear: "[I do] not [?]"
And when they had finished mocking him, they stripped the purple robe off him, clothed him in his own garments, and led him out to crucify him.
And they forced a certain passer-by, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the field, the father of Alexander and Rufus, into service, so that he would carry his cross.
And they brought him to Golgotha, a place whose name translated means "the Place of the Skull."
And they gave him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he did not take it.
And they crucified him and divided his garments, and cast lots over them to see who would take what.
And it was the third hour when they crucified him.
And the charge against him was written above: "This is the King of the Jews."
And with him they crucified two robbers, one on his right and one on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled which says: "He was counted among the lawless."
And those who passed by reviled him, shaking their heads and saying: "Aha! You who would destroy the temple and build it again on the third day,
save yourself and come down from the cross!"
In the same way the chief priests, together with the scribes, mocked him among themselves and said: "He saved others; he cannot save himself.
Christ, King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe you." And those who had been crucified with him also taunted him.
And when it was about the sixth hour, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said: "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" which translated means: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
And when some of those standing by heard it, they said: "Look, he is calling Elijah."
And they ran, filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, and they said: "Wait, let us see whether Elijah will come to take him down."
But Jesus let out a cry and breathed his last.
And the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.
When the centurion who was standing by him saw that he had cried out and breathed his last, he said: "Truly this man was the Son of God."
And there were also women there, watching from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the Less and of Joses, and Salome,
who, while he was still in Galilee, had followed him at once, and many other women who had come to Jerusalem.
And when evening came — for it was Friday, which is the day before the Sabbath —
Joseph of Arimathea came, an honorable counselor, for he too was waiting for the kingdom of God. He dared to go in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
But Pilate was surprised that he had died so soon, and he summoned the executioner and asked him: "Did he die so soon?"
And when he learned it from the executioner, he granted the body to Joseph.
And right there he bought linen cloth, and he laid him in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Joses saw where they were laying him.
And when the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they could come and anoint him.
And very early in the morning on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb just as the sun was rising.
And they were saying to one another: "Who will roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?"
And they looked up and saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was very large.
And they went into the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white garment, and they were amazed.
And he said to them: "Do not be afraid! You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look, there is the place where they laid him.
Now go and tell his disciples: He is going ahead of you to Galilee, and there you will see him, as he told you."
And when they heard this, they went out and fled from the tomb, for they were frightened and astonished. And they told no one, for they were afraid.
